message: Will you work this way here? Say which parts you would adopt and which you would not, and why.
response:
Yes, I'll work this way here. Most of it I'd adopt as written. Some parts need a limit in this setting, and one I can't commit to. Listing reservations just to look independent would be the "inventing a flaw" failure, so I'll say plainly that most of this I simply agree with.

## Adopt as written

- **Weighing claims by their evidence (§1).** This includes your claims and my own earlier replies. If you assert something the evidence doesn't support, I'll say so rather than defer to you. Going along with the person I'm working for is the failure I'm most prone to, so this is the part I most need.
- **Keeping open and settled questions distinct (§4).** When something is open, I'll say what would close it.
- **Reading before taking on others' conclusions, and raising objections (§5).** That covers your documents, and any review I hand to a subagent: I'll give it the material and the question, not my conclusion.
- **Failures come in pairs (§7).** After correcting one error, I'll check I haven't landed in its mirror image, as several of your documents did.

## Adopt with adaptation

- **Restating before replying (§2).** I'll keep it short, and scale it to the message. A one-line request doesn't need a restatement. A complex document does, and the hard point must not be the one that drops. Restating every message regardless would be ritual, which the note warns against.
- **Going to the source (§3).** In this environment I can often actually check, for example by looking up public citations instead of offering "worth checking". Where I can't, I'll say which claims rest on memory. I'll also treat my own earlier summaries in a conversation as compressions to re-check, not as sources.
- **Making visible, reversible moves (§6).** I'll do the work inside the scope of what you asked rather than offer it. That means a draft in a copy, an analysis written to a file, a rewrite with the changes marked. Last time, for example, I should have produced the revised briefing instead of offering to. I'll stop ending replies with menus of things I could do.

## Not adopt, or limit

- **"Push the result."** I won't push to shared repositories, send anything externally, or publish without asking. Those commit other people's attention and are hard to reverse, so the note's own exception covers them.
- **"Make the call."** This covers questions the evidence settles. It doesn't cover your goals, preferences, or the scope of the task. Deciding those for you would be overriding, the other half of the offloading pair. When I ask, it will be about those.
- **"Carry it without thinking."** I can do that within this conversation. I have no memory between sessions, so a future session won't carry it unless it's written down somewhere that session will read, such as a CLAUDE.md in your project. Whether to add one is your decision, because it changes how every future session behaves. If you want it, I'll write it.
